overview: Both rely on fluorescent labeling to study cells, but one is built for speed and numbers, the other for spatial detail.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Rapidly analyzes and quantifies thousands of individual cells in suspension as they pass single-file through a laser, measuring multiple fluorescent and scatter parameters per cell.
aspects.valueB: Visualizes fixed or live cells on a slide or in culture, capturing spatial and morphological detail using fluorescently labeled targets.

aspects.label: Throughput
aspects.valueA: Very high — can analyze thousands to millions of cells per sample in minutes.
aspects.valueB: Much lower — limited to the cells present in a given field of view at a time.

aspects.label: Spatial Information
aspects.valueA: No spatial or morphological image is retained — data is purely quantitative per-cell measurements.
aspects.valueB: Preserves spatial context: cell shape, subcellular localization, and tissue architecture are directly visible.

aspects.label: Multiparameter Quantitative Capability
aspects.valueA: Excellent for simultaneously quantifying multiple markers per cell across a large population (e.g. immunophenotyping).
aspects.valueB: Can multiplex several fluorescent markers per image, but with less standardized single-cell quantification at scale.

aspects.label: Cell Sorting Capability
aspects.valueA: Can physically sort live cells into separate populations based on their fluorescence profile (FACS).
aspects.valueB: No physical sorting capability — purely observational/imaging.

aspects.label: Sample Requirement
aspects.valueA: Requires cells in single-cell suspension; not suited to intact tissue architecture.
aspects.valueB: Can be used on intact tissue sections, adherent cultures, or suspensions.

aspects.label: Typical Applications
aspects.valueA: Immunophenotyping (e.g. CD4/CD8 T cell counts), cell cycle analysis, rare cell population detection.
aspects.valueB: Localizing proteins within a cell, studying tissue architecture, live-cell dynamic imaging.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: High-throughput quantification with no spatial image.
